questions.stem: What happens to a light ray when it enters from a rarer medium to a denser medium?
choices: It bends away from the normal
It continues in the same direction
questions.solution: When a light ray enters from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it slows down and bends towards the normal. This is because the speed of light is higher in a rarer medium. A pupil who confuses the direction of bending might think it bends away from the normal. Others might think it reflects back or continues in the same direction, which is incorrect.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the central point of a lens?
questions.solution: The term used to describe the central point of a lens is the optical centre, which is the point through which light rays pass undeviated. The principal axis is a line passing through the optical centre and the centres of curvature, not the central point itself. The principal focus is where parallel rays converge after passing through the lens, and the centre of curvature refers to the centre of the spherical surfaces of the lens.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the image formed by a concave lens?
choices: It is always real and inverted
It is always virtual and inverted
It is always virtual and erect

questions.solution: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image, irrespective of the position of the object. The correct option is 'It is always virtual and erect'. The other options are incorrect because a concave lens never forms a real image, and it always forms an erect image.

questions.stem: What is the reason we are able to see objects around us?
choices: Because objects produce their own light
questions.solution: The correct answer is because objects reflect light. When light hits an object, some of it bounces off and enters our eyes, allowing us to see the object. Objects do not always produce their own light, they do not absorb light to be visible, and not all objects emit light.

questions.stem: A convex lens is used to form an image of an object. If the object is placed at twice the focal length of the lens, what will be the nature of the image?
questions.solution: When an object is placed at twice the focal length of a convex lens, the image formed is real and inverted. This follows from the lens formula and the nature of convex lenses. The other options are incorrect because a convex lens does not produce a virtual image when the object is placed at twice the focal length, and the image cannot be erect in this case.

questions.stem: A ray of light is incident on a convex lens. If the object is placed at the focal point of the lens, what will be the nature of the image formed?

questions.stem: A student places an object between the pole and the principal focus of a concave mirror. What type of image is formed?
questions.solution: When an object is placed between the pole and the principal focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays diverge and appear to come from a point behind the mirror, forming a virtual and erect image. Real images are formed when light rays actually converge, which does not happen in this case. A real image would be inverted, and an erect real image is not possible with a concave mirror. A virtual and inverted image would require different conditions, such as a convex mirror or a different object position.

mr.stem: एका विद्यार्थीने अवतल दर्पणाच्या ध्रुव आणि मुख्य फोकस यामध्ये वस्तू ठेवली. कोणत्या प्रकारचे छायाचित्र तयार होते?
mr.solution: जेव्हा वस्तू अवतल दर्पणाच्या ध्रुव आणि मुख्य फोकस यामध्ये ठेवली जाते, तेव्हा परावर्तित किरण विस्तारतात आणि दर्पणाच्या पाठीमागे एका बिंदूपासून येणारे असे वाटते, जे काल्पनिक आणि उलटे छायाचित्र तयार करते. खरे छायाचित्र तयार होतात जेव्हा प्रकाश किरण खरोखर एकत्र येतात, जे या परिस्थितीत होत नाही. खरे छायाचित्र उलटे असतात, आणि अवतल दर्पणासाठी उलटे नसलेले खरे छायाचित्र शक्य नाही. काल्पनिक आणि उलटे छायाचित्र वेगळ्या परिस्थितीत आवश्यक असतात, जसे की उत्तल दर्पण किंवा वस्तूच्या वेगळ्या ठिकाणावर.
